# Deploying to Production
## Last Updated: 2025-08-15

### Prerequisites
- Access to the deployment dashboard (https://deploy.internal.company.com)
- VPN connected to production network
- Deployment approval from team lead

### Steps
1. Create a release branch from `main`
2. Run the full test suite: `make test-all`
3. Build the Docker image: `docker build -t app:release .`
4. Push to ECR: `docker push 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/app:release`
5. Open the deployment dashboard and select the new image
6. Deploy to canary (5% traffic) and monitor for 15 minutes
7. If metrics are green, promote to full rollout
8. Notify #releases Slack channel

### Rollback
If issues are detected, use the dashboard to revert to the previous version.

### Related Docs
- See [Monitoring Guide](kb/monitoring-guide.md) for what to watch during deployment
- See [Incident Response](kb/incident-response-plan.md) if something goes wrong
- See [Database Migrations](kb/database-migrations.md) for DB changes during deploy

# Production Deployment Guide
## Last Updated: 2026-01-10

### Overview
This guide covers how to deploy services to production using our CI/CD pipeline.

### Prerequisites
- GitHub access with write permissions to the repo
- AWS CLI configured with deployment role
- Approval from engineering manager (not team lead)

### Deployment Process
1. Merge your PR to `main` branch
2. CI/CD pipeline automatically builds and tests
3. Pipeline pushes Docker image to ECR with git SHA tag
4. ArgoCD detects the new image and initiates canary deployment
5. Canary runs for 30 minutes with 10% traffic
6. If Datadog metrics pass thresholds, ArgoCD promotes to full rollout
7. Post in #deployments Slack channel (not #releases)

### Manual Rollback
```bash
argocd app rollback catalog-api --to-revision <previous>
```

### Port Configuration
- Production API: port 8080
- Health check: port 8081/healthz
- Metrics: port 9090/metrics

### Related Docs
- See [Monitoring Setup](kb/monitoring-setup.md) for dashboard access
- See [Runbook: Service Recovery](kb/service-recovery-runbook.md) for incident handling

# Onboarding Guide for New Engineers
## Last Updated: 2025-11-01

### Week 1: Setup
1. Get laptop from IT (Mac or Linux, your choice)
2. Set up development environment using `setup.sh` script
3. Request access to: GitHub, Jira, Slack, AWS Console, Jenkins
4. Complete security training in LMS
5. Read the Architecture Overview doc (kb/architecture-overview.md)

### Week 1: Tools
- **IDE**: VS Code (recommended) or IntelliJ
- **CI/CD**: Jenkins (legacy) — we're migrating to GitHub Actions
- **Monitoring**: Grafana dashboards at https://grafana.internal.company.com
- **Logging**: ELK stack at https://kibana.internal.company.com
- **Deployment**: See [Deploying to Production](kb/deploying-to-production.md)

### Week 2: Codebase
1. Clone the monorepo: `git clone git@github.com:company/monorepo.git`
2. Run locally: `docker-compose up`
3. Read service README files
4. Pair with your buddy on a small task

### Week 2: Architecture
- Frontend: React app served from CloudFront
- Backend: Python microservices on ECS
- Database: PostgreSQL (primary), Redis (cache)
- Message queue: RabbitMQ
- Search: Elasticsearch

### Week 3-4: First PR
- Pick a "good first issue" from Jira
- Follow the PR template and code review process
- Deploy your first change (with buddy supervision)

### Key Contacts
- Engineering Manager: Sarah Kim (sarah@company.com)
- DevOps Lead: Alex Rivera (alex@company.com)
- Architecture questions: James Wong (james@company.com)
- Security questions: Lisa Chen (lisa@company.com)

# API Reference v2
## Last Updated: 2026-02-01

### Base URL
Production: https://api.company.com/v2
Staging: https://api-staging.company.com/v2

### Authentication
All requests require a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
```
Authorization: Bearer <api_key>
```

### Endpoints

#### GET /users
List all users. Supports pagination.
- Query params: `page` (default: 1), `per_page` (default: 20, max: 100)
- Response: `{"users": [...], "total": 150, "page": 1}`

#### GET /users/:id
Get a single user by ID.
- Response: `{"id": 1, "name": "...", "email": "..."}`

#### POST /users
Create a new user.
- Body: `{"name": "string", "email": "string", "role": "string"}`
- Response: 201 with created user

#### GET /products
List products. Supports filtering and pagination.
- Query params: `category`, `min_price`, `max_price`, `page`, `per_page`
- Response: `{"products": [...], "total": 500}`

#### POST /orders
Create a new order.
- Body: `{"items": [{"product_id": 1, "quantity": 2}]}`
- Requires authentication
- Response: 201 with order details

### Rate Limits
- Authenticated: 1000 requests/minute
- Unauthenticated: 100 requests/minute

### Error Codes
- 400: Bad Request
- 401: Unauthorized
- 403: Forbidden
- 404: Not Found
- 429: Too Many Requests
- 500: Internal Server Error

### Ports
- API: port 3000
- WebSocket: port 3001

# Architecture Overview
## Last Updated: 2025-06-01

### System Diagram
```
CloudFront -> ALB -> ECS (microservices) -> PostgreSQL / Redis / RabbitMQ
```

### Services
1. **api-gateway**: Routes external requests to internal services. Port 8080.
2. **user-service**: Handles user CRUD, authentication. Port 8081.
3. **catalog-service**: Product catalog management. Port 8082.
4. **order-service**: Order processing and fulfillment. Port 8083.
5. **notification-service**: Email, SMS, push notifications. Port 8084.
6. **search-service**: Elasticsearch-backed search. Port 8085.

### Data Stores
- **PostgreSQL 14**: Primary database, hosted on RDS
- **Redis 6**: Session cache and rate limiting
- **RabbitMQ 3.11**: Async message processing
- **Elasticsearch 7.17**: Full-text search

### Infrastructure
- **AWS Region**: us-east-1 (primary), us-west-2 (DR)
- **Compute**: ECS Fargate
- **CI/CD**: Jenkins (migrating to GitHub Actions Q2 2025)
- **Monitoring**: Grafana + Prometheus
- **Logging**: ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana)

### Communication
- Synchronous: REST over HTTP between services
- Asynchronous: RabbitMQ for event-driven workflows
- All internal communication uses mTLS

### Deployment
- See [Deploying to Production](kb/deploying-to-production.md) for deployment process
- Blue-green deployment strategy
- Canary releases for high-risk changes

# Database Guide
## Last Updated: 2025-09-20

### Connection Details
- Production: `postgresql://readonly@prod-db.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com:5432/appdb`
- Staging: `postgresql://dev@staging-db.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com:5432/appdb`
- Local: `postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/appdb`

### Schema Overview
- `users` - User accounts and profiles
- `products` - Product catalog
- `orders` - Order records
- `order_items` - Line items for orders
- `notifications` - Notification queue and history
- `audit_log` - Access audit trail

### Migrations
We use Alembic for database migrations.
```bash
alembic upgrade head        # Apply all pending migrations
alembic revision --autogenerate -m "description"  # Create new migration
alembic downgrade -1        # Rollback last migration
```

### Best Practices
- Always test migrations on staging first
- Large migrations should run during maintenance window (Sundays 2-4 AM UTC)
- Never run DDL changes directly on production
- See [Database Migrations](kb/database-migrations.md) for detailed migration process

### Backup Schedule
- Automated snapshots: every 6 hours
- Point-in-time recovery: up to 7 days
- Cross-region backup: daily to us-west-2

### Performance
- Connection pool: max 200 connections per service
- Slow query threshold: 500ms (logged to Datadog)
- Index recommendations reviewed monthly

# Security Practices
## Last Updated: 2026-01-15

### Authentication
- All services use JWT tokens for authentication
- Tokens expire after 1 hour
- Refresh tokens valid for 30 days
- MFA required for admin accounts
- SSO via Okta for internal tools

### Secrets Management
- All secrets stored in AWS Secrets Manager
- No hardcoded secrets in code (enforced by pre-commit hooks)
- Secret rotation: API keys every 90 days, DB passwords every 180 days

### Network Security
- All services in private VPC subnets
- Public access only through CloudFront + ALB
- WAF rules for common attack patterns (SQLi, XSS)
- Internal service communication uses mTLS

### Data Protection
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 for all databases
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.3
- PII fields additionally encrypted at application level
- Data classification policy: see [Data Classification](kb/data-classification.md)

### Incident Response
- See [Incident Response Plan](kb/incident-response-plan.md) for procedures
- On-call rotation managed in PagerDuty
- Escalation path: On-call -> Team Lead -> Engineering Manager -> CTO

### Compliance
- SOC 2 Type II certified (renewed annually)
- GDPR compliant for EU customers
- Annual penetration testing by external firm
- Bug bounty program via HackerOne

### Monitoring Ports
- Prometheus metrics: port 9090
- Health checks: port 8081

# Troubleshooting Guide
## Last Updated: 2025-07-10

### Common Issues

#### Service Won't Start
1. Check Docker logs: `docker logs <container_id>`
2. Verify environment variables are set correctly
3. Check database connectivity: `psql -h <host> -U <user> -d appdb`
4. Ensure Redis is running: `redis-cli ping`

#### High Latency
1. Check Grafana dashboards for CPU/memory spikes
2. Look at database slow query log in Kibana
3. Check RabbitMQ queue depth
4. Verify no circuit breakers are open

#### Deployment Failures
1. Check Jenkins build logs
2. Verify Docker image built successfully
3. Check ECS task definition for errors
4. Verify IAM roles have correct permissions

#### Database Connection Issues
- Check connection pool status: `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;`
- Max connections per service: 100 (note: this differs from database-guide.md which says 200)
- Connection timeout: 30 seconds
- Verify security group allows traffic from service subnet

#### Authentication Failures
- Verify JWT token is not expired
- Check Okta configuration
- Ensure user has correct role assignments
- Check auth-service logs at port 8081 (same port as health checks — potential conflict)

### Monitoring
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal.company.com
- Kibana: https://kibana.internal.company.com
- PagerDuty: https://company.pagerduty.com

### Escalation
- P1 (service down): Page on-call immediately
- P2 (degraded): Slack #incidents, on-call responds within 30 min
- P3 (minor): Create Jira ticket, address in next sprint

### Related Docs
- [Monitoring Setup](kb/monitoring-setup.md)
- [Incident Response Plan](kb/incident-response-plan.md)
- [Service Recovery Runbook](kb/service-recovery-runbook.md)

# API Reference v1 (DEPRECATED)
## Last Updated: 2024-12-01
## STATUS: DEPRECATED - Use v2. Migration guide: kb/v1-to-v2-migration.md

### Base URL
Production: https://api.company.com/v1

### Note
v1 endpoints will be sunset on March 31, 2026. All clients should migrate to v2.

### Endpoints

#### GET /users
List all users. No pagination support.
- Response: `{"users": [...]}`

#### GET /users/:id
Get a single user.
- Response: `{"id": 1, "name": "...", "email": "..."}`

#### GET /products
List all products. No filtering.
- Response: `{"products": [...]}`

### Differences from v2
- No pagination
- No rate limiting
- No WebSocket support
- Authentication uses API keys in query string (less secure)

### Port
- API: port 3000 (same as v2)
